target_audience: High school AP Calculus students or University freshmen

sections.title: The Hook: Explicit vs. Implicit
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'Explicit' functions (y is isolated, like a recipe) vs. 'Implicit' relations (x and y are tangled, like a knot). Use a visual comparison between a straight line and a circle. Explain that while we can't always solve for y, we still need to find the slope (dy/dx).
sections.example: Explicit: y = x² + 1 (A clear path). Implicit: x² + y² = 25 (A circle where x and y are locked together).

sections.title: Prerequisite Check: The Chain Rule Engine
sections.content: Quickly review the Chain Rule, as it is the 'engine' of implicit differentiation. Emphasize that when we differentiate a term with 'y' with respect to 'x', we must treat y as a nested function y(x). Visual: A 'y' box inside a larger function box.
sections.example: If we differentiate y³ with respect to x, it becomes 3y² · (dy/dx). Think of (dy/dx) as the 'tail' that follows every y-differentiation.

sections.title: The Three-Step Recipe
sections.content: Outline the logical workflow: 1. Differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to x. 2. Collect all terms containing (dy/dx) on one side. 3. Factor out (dy/dx) and solve. Use an animation of moving algebraic terms across an equals sign.
sections.example: For x² + y² = 25: Step 1 gives 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0. Step 2 moves 2x: 2y(dy/dx) = -2x. Step 3 divides: dy/dx = -x/y.

sections.title: Guided Application: The Robotic Arm
sections.content: Apply the concept to a 'Robot Arm' scenario. Imagine a mechanical arm pinned at the origin, tracing a curve. To find the direction the 'hand' is moving at a specific point, we need the derivative at that exact coordinate (x, y).
sections.example: Find the slope of the curve x³ + y³ = 6xy (Folium of Descartes) at the point (3, 3). Show the 'hand' of the robot at (3,3) and calculate the tangent slope being -1.

sections.title: Visual Verification & Summary
sections.content: Display a graph of the implicit relation with the tangent line drawn at the example point. This reinforces that (dy/dx) represents the physical 'steepness' even in complex shapes. Summarize: Treat y as a function, use the chain rule, and isolate the derivative.
sections.example: Visual: A glowing tangent line touching the circle at (3, 4). As the point moves, the 'dy/dx = -x/y' formula updates the slope value in real-time.
